_comment: Hand-maintained offer catalog, activated by the 'Import catalog from file'
button in /admin. Built from the olmem-tech repo's authoritative definitions
and verified against the live pages listed in each offer's evidence_urls.
Importing costs nothing - no crawl, no LLM call. When the site's offers change,
edit this file and click Import again. The catalog version hashes these offers, so
an edit forces affected prospects to be rescored rather than pitched a stale offer.
Every entry in allowed_claims must be verifiable on a page in evidence_urls. The
drafting step may not exceed them.
Discovery controls, per offer:
search_queries   - the seeds sent to Tavily.
region_scoped    - true appends each region in DISCOVERY_REGIONS, which is how
local trades and regional manufacturers are found. False
searches the query as written; an online seller has no service
area, and adding a state returns the local retail counter.
discovery_weight - share of each run's query budget. Zero parks an offer: still
in the catalog and still pitchable, but no budget is spent
looking for it.
Each run takes max(10, MAX_DISCOVERIES_PER_RUN * 2) queries, split by weight and
rotated by date, so consecutive runs explore different parts of the space.
Current focus: every offer is active. Contractor work keeps the largest share
because it is the highest-volume market; ERP and the enterprise tiers carry less
budget because they are lower-volume, higher-value, and need fewer prospects.

offers.name: Olmem ERP (Manufacturing)
offers.summary: A maintenance-first manufacturing ERP for small and mid-sized manufacturers — the ones without an IT department. The software is a licensing product: bought once, owned permanently, with no subscription and no per-seat fees. Support and custom development exist only as optional add-on services for businesses that want them. It replaces two situations: a per-seat SaaS bill for a system the manufacturer will never own, or no system at all beyond spreadsheets and a few disconnected programs.
problems_solved: A per-seat ERP or MRP subscription costs more every year and leaves the manufacturer owning nothing
Adding plant floor or office staff to the current system means paying for more seats
The subscription must be renewed indefinitely or the business loses access to its own operating system
Production and maintenance data sit on a vendor's servers rather than with the manufacturer
Modules the manufacturer does not use are bundled into the price anyway
Production, inventory, and maintenance are tracked in separate Excel files that do not reconcile
Several disconnected programs each hold part of the picture and none of them talk to each other
Preventive maintenance is missed because no system schedules or escalates it
There is no maintenance history, so the same machine failures keep recurring undiagnosed
Nobody can answer what a finished job actually cost, because the data was never captured
Stock levels are wrong because there is no ledger behind them, only a spreadsheet someone edits
There is no audit trail behind inventory movements or work order changes
ideal_customer_signals: Family-owned or owner-operated manufacturer, often describing a second or third generation
One facility, or a small number of plants all within one region
Owner, founder, or a named individual presented as the point of contact
A stated team size in the tens rather than the hundreds
Regional or national customer base rather than a global one
No IT department implied anywhere on the site
Careers or job listings requiring experience with a named ERP or MRP subscription platform
Job postings referencing 'our ERP system', MRP, or a named inventory or scheduling SaaS
A customer or vendor portal link pointing at a third-party SaaS domain rather than their own
Job listings requiring advanced Excel or spreadsheet proficiency for planning, scheduling, or inventory roles
Pages instructing customers to call or email to check stock, lead time, or order status
Order forms published as downloadable PDF or Excel files rather than an online system
A stated manual quote or order turnaround measured in days
No customer portal, order tracking, or online ordering anywhere on the site
Machine shop, fabricator, molder, processor, or assembler with maintained equipment
Careers pages hiring maintenance technicians, production planners, or schedulers
Quality or compliance certifications implying record-keeping and traceability obligations
exclusion_signals: Publicly traded, or an investor relations, shareholder, or SEC filings section on the site
A subsidiary, division, or portfolio company of a larger corporate group
Locations on more than one continent, or described as a global manufacturer
A stated headcount in the hundreds or thousands, or many plants across several regions
Job listings for in-house IT, ERP administrator, or systems analyst roles, implying an internal team that owns the stack
A dedicated procurement or vendor-onboarding process described on the site
The business already owns a perpetual-license system deployed on its own infrastructure, so the subscription pain does not apply
The business is itself a software vendor, ERP reseller, or systems integrator
No production, inventory, or maintenance operation to manage
The site indicates the business is closing, sold, or winding down
allowed_claims: Olmem ERP is a one-time purchase — you buy the license once and own the software permanently
No subscription is ever required to keep running
There are no per-seat fees and users are unlimited, so adding staff costs nothing extra
Unlimited company data is included
It is one system for maintenance, production, and the whole operation
It is a maintenance-first platform built for small and mid-sized manufacturers
It uses a desktop-first architecture with local deployment, data ownership, and role-based permissions
Founding-customer pricing starts at $9,500 one-time with installation included, against a regular price of $19,500
Professional installation and setup, database setup and configuration, and employee setup and initial training are all included in the one-time license price
Annual support is an optional add-on service, not a condition of ownership — the ERP keeps working whether it is never purchased at all or bought once and later allowed to lapse
If a business wants the optional support add-on, it is $2,925 to $3,900 per year, 15 to 20 percent of the license
Custom development is an optional add-on, available from $175 per hour and scoped only if it is asked for
A live demo is available at erpdemo.olmemtech.com
